title: The welcome-screen mascot — asked again with real-screen numbers

steps.path: The mascot on the screen with no session open
steps.headline: Now that the real screen shows the mascot's motion is the main cost, which do you want?
steps.today: On the welcome screen the mascot breathes and sways nonstop. You answered "Leave it as is" when I described the cost as mostly the frosted-glass blur.
steps.problem: Measured on your real screen, idle on the welcome screen: the graphics chip is 36% busy (8% with the mascot hidden, 30% with the blur off), and the app uses about half a processor core. So the blur is a small part; the nonstop motion is most of it, so other mascot themes likely pay it too (measured on yours only) — battery and heat while nothing is happening.
steps.proposal: Pick one. Your earlier answer still stands if you pick Leave it.

options.label: The mascot settles after a while
pros: After ~10 quiet seconds it comes to rest; idle cost drops to about zero
It moves again the moment you move the mouse or anything happens
cons: A still mascot on a screen left alone
You once said a buddy that stops breathing looks lifeless

options.label: Keep it moving, but at a lower frame rate
pros: Lower cost — how much lower is not measured yet
cons: Motion looks a little less smooth; you've called stepped motion juddery before

options.label: Leave it as is
cons: About a third of the graphics chip and half a core while the welcome screen sits idle
